claim: Contrastive semantic similarity (CSS) derived from CLIP text encoders encodes more semantic information for text pairs than NLI logits, enabling more accurate uncertainty estimation in LLMs.
falsifier: Replace CSS features with NLI logits in the same uncertainty estimation pipeline and compare AUROC or accuracy/rejection trade-off on held-out QA datasets.

conditions: uncertainty estimation performed by spectral clustering on semantic similarity features
exclusions: limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished

title: Contrastive semantic similarity–accuracy of uncertainty estimation…

claim: Under the assumptions of local existence for both relativistic and classical Euler equations, the difference between the relativistic solution (number density n0, temperature T0) and the classical solution (density ρ, temperature θ) is bounded by the difference between the classical and relativistic solutions plus a term of order 1/c^2, with constants independent of c.
falsifier: One can numerically compute solutions of both systems for large c and verify that the difference scales as 1/c^2.

conditions: local existence of both solutions on [0,T]
initial data sufficiently close to constant states
exclusions: limited to the regime where both relativistic and classical Euler equations have local classical solutions and the initial data are small perturbations of constant states

title: Increasing the speed–convergence of relativistic solution principle
